correctness.rationale: Composing the wet and dry flows gives k[U−f_c(T−δ)]/A = 2−b−bac−(1−b)(a+c), with a=exp(−kt₁), c=exp(−kt₂), b=exp(−hδ). At fixed internal gap ac is fixed and the arithmetic–geometric mean inequality uniquely gives a=c. Define B(z)=z(1−z)+r(1−z)². The reduced objective has G′/A=−η−z+bB and G″/A=−(kz/2)(1−bB′)−hbB<0 because B≥0 and B′<1 on the feasible z-range. G′(T)=−f_c−A; the left slope divided by A is r(1−z₀)²−z₀²−η, strictly increasing from −1−η to r−η as T grows. Its root for r>η rationalizes to the stated z_c, including r=1; equality at T_c still gives a unique zero gap. A zero gap has arbitrary bookkeeping splits of one physical wet interval. For the interior solution, ∂_T G′=(Akz/2)(1−bB′)>0 and stationarity implies η=bB−z≤b(B−z)<br. This proves monotonicity and the strict bound; hence z tends to 0 and stationarity gives the stated limiting rest. At onset the ratio ∂_T G′/(−G″) reduces to the displayed coefficient after using 1−B′=2[z+r(1−z)]. The exact logarithmic benchmark follows by substitution. This is a fixed clock horizon with capacity-saturating weather, initially recovered capacity and no carried ponding or fixed dose. The frozen verification notes and script were inspected, not executed; the result is obtained analytically.

value.rationale: A practical modeling choice becomes an exact mathematical decision: when an interruption is worth sacrificing capacity-saturating wet time. The threshold replaces a continuous timing search, proves when no rest can ever pay, and gives quantitative onset and saturation of the unique rest when it does pay. This is useful within the two-pulse model, without implying anything about fixed-dose irrigation, richer soils, or schedules with more pulses.
